note: NO MIGRATION WAS PERFORMED. This is an assessment only, per the hard-locked stack decision.

assessments.subject: Astro
assessments.compatibility: Astro 6 already requires Node >=22.12.0 (confirmed in CHANGELOG.md, PR #14427) — so this repo's current Node 22 engine requirement is unaffected by the 6->7 jump specifically.
breakingChanges: HTML whitespace stripping now follows JSX rules by default (removes insignificant whitespace/line breaks around elements). Could subtly change rendered spacing in any component relying on incidental whitespace-as-a-space between inline elements.
@astrojs/db package removed entirely (was deprecated in 6.4.5). Repo does not use it (grep confirmed no @astrojs/db reference in package.json/astro.config.mjs) — not applicable.
Go-based compiler and experimental.rustCompiler flag removed. Repo's astro.config.mjs does not set this flag — not applicable.
assessments.workRequired: Upgrade astro dependency; re-run full visual regression (Stage 15 baselines) to catch any whitespace-stripping-induced spacing change; re-run npm run check and npm run build.
assessments.risk: LOW-MEDIUM — no removed feature this repo uses, but the whitespace-stripping change is a real behavioral change that visual regression, not type-checking, would catch.
assessments.validation: npm run check && npm run build; Stage 15 site-baselines.json diff against a pre-migration snapshot on all 4 sampled routes x 6 viewports.
assessments.status: VERIFY-BLOCKED for GO/NO-GO — requires actually running the upgrade in an isolated branch to observe real whitespace diffs, which is out of this project's scope.

assessments.subject: TypeScript
assessments.target: 7.0.2 (published under @typescript/native-preview during preview; `tsc` binary name reserved for "7.0 RC and later" per upstream README)
assessments.compatibility: TypeScript 7 ("tsgo") is NOT an incremental tsc release — it is a from-scratch native Go port of the compiler. The official README confirms the preview is currently distributed under a DIFFERENT package name (@typescript/native-preview), with `tsc` itself reserved for a later RC.
breakingChanges: Entirely different compiler implementation. Plugin/tooling ecosystem compatibility (astro-check, editor integration, prettier-plugin-astro type-aware rules if any) is unproven for a native-Go compiler.
@astrojs/check (this repo's astro check tool) compatibility with a Go-based tsc is unverified — this repo's primary correctness gate depends on it.
assessments.workRequired: Wait for a stable, non-preview release under the `typescript` package name and verify @astrojs/check compatibility before considering this upgrade at all.
assessments.risk: HIGH — this is the single highest-risk item in the target stack. The project's entire correctness gate (npm run check) is astro check, which wraps tsc; an incompatible or behaviorally-different compiler could silently change what passes and what fails.
assessments.validation: Full npm run check pass/fail comparison against the current 143-hint baseline (established this session) BEFORE and AFTER, on an isolated branch, before any consideration of merging.
assessments.status: NO-GO for now — the preview status and package-name mismatch alone are sufficient reason to defer this upgrade independent of any other factor.

assessments.subject: Cloudflare Pages -> Workers (@astrojs/cloudflare)
assessments.current: Cloudflare Pages Functions (functions/ directory, wrangler.jsonc assets binding)
assessments.compatibility: VERIFY-BLOCKED — the actual @astrojs/cloudflare adapter changelog/migration guide was not fetched this session. This is a full deployment-model change (Pages Functions to Workers is a different runtime/routing model, not a version bump), independent of the Astro version.
breakingChanges: functions/api/chat.js and functions/api/contact.js (Cloudflare Pages Functions) would need to become Worker route handlers — a structural rewrite, not a config change.
wrangler.jsonc's assets binding and preview/production env split would need reworking for Workers deployment semantics.
The existing CI workflow (.github/workflows/deploy.yml, cloudflare/pages-action@v1) targets Pages specifically and would need replacement.
assessments.workRequired: A dedicated migration project: rewrite functions/, reconfigure wrangler.jsonc, replace the CI deploy job, re-verify the AI chat endpoint (Workers AI binding) and MailChannels contact form end-to-end against a live Workers deployment.
assessments.risk: HIGH — this is infrastructure, not code. A failed migration here means a broken production chat widget or broken contact form on a live dental practice site.
assessments.validation: Full functional test of /api/chat and /api/contact against a Workers preview deployment before any production cutover; this cannot be validated from within this harness.
assessments.status: NO-GO for this project — explicitly out of scope per the hard-locked stack decision, and the evidence above shows why it would need to be its own dedicated project regardless.

overallRecommendation: Stay on the current stack. Of the 6 items assessed, only the Astro 6->7 bump has no other blocking factor (low-medium risk, real but boundable via visual regression); every other item is either explicitly out of scope, has insufficient live evidence gathered this session, or is actively NO-GO (TypeScript 7 preview status, Workers/TinaCMS architectural scope).
